text: High-frequency trading firms spent tens of millions laying microwave links between Chicago and New Jersey along a route already served by fibre. What were they buying?
choices: Greater bandwidth than fibre could provide
Lower latency, because radio through air propagates faster than light through glass
Freedom from the ISP's traffic shaping
explanation: Air has a refractive index of essentially 1.0 while fibre is about 1.468, so a microwave path propagates roughly 45% faster than the same distance of glass. They were buying the difference between c and c/1.468 — a few milliseconds — and microwave carries far less bandwidth than fibre, so it was purely a latency purchase.
